metadata.title: APPSC EO Grade-III — Special Topic Notes: Sources of Income & Allocation of Temple Funds
metadata.statutoryFocus: Section 57 — Budget of Charitable or Religious Institution or Endowment
metadata.exam: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III, Endowments Department
metadata.paper: Paper II — Hindu Philosophy and Temple System

sectionCoverage: Submission of the budget to the competent authority
Mandatory budget provisions and expenditure priorities
Limits on salaries of religious and secular establishment
Allocations for pilgrim safety and convenience
Contributions to the institution's reserve fund
Provisions for construction, repairs and renovation
Contribution towards the Common Good Fund
Alterations made by the competent authority
Reporting and possible ratification of excess expenditure
eoResponsibilities: Estimating next year's income and expenditure
Checking expected income from Hundi offerings, donations, services, property, and investments
Ensuring sufficient funds for worship, rituals, Dittam, and essential staff
Providing for existing liabilities and contracts
Budgeting for pilgrim amenities, sanitation, water, safety, and convenience
Monitoring whether expenditure stays within sanctioned heads
Obtaining approval for a revised budget when necessary
Reporting expenditure beyond the approved budget
Maintaining financial records for scrutiny and audit
part1_overview.corePrinciple: Temple money is institutional money. It must be applied to authorised purposes, not treated as the personal money of the trustee or EO.

items: Kanukas and offerings made by devotees
Offerings in kind, where legally received and accounted for
Donations for specified religious or charitable purposes
Gifts of movable or immovable property
Donations received from philanthropists or other permitted donors
Archana or other permitted service charges
Special darshan or other authorised service receipts
Income from other lawfully leased institutional properties
Donations or contributions from eligible institutions or persons
Receipts from medical or charitable services
Income from other permitted institutional activities
Income arising from property, money or assets dedicated to a particular religious or charitable purpose

part3_section_57_1_budget_preparation.definition: A forward-looking estimate of probable receipts + probable disbursements for the following financial year.
part3_section_57_1_budget_preparation.deadline: 90 days before the close of every financial year
part3_section_57_1_budget_preparation.note: Section 6(d) covers Maths irrespective of income classification.

clause_i_maintenance_worship_services.salaryCeiling: Salaries of religious and secular establishment <= 30% of annual income calculated under Section 65

coverage: Sufficient available funds for day-to-day financial continuity

clause_iv_health_safety_convenience.minimumAllocation: At least 40% of the balance remaining after provisions for items (i), (ii) and (iii)

clause_v_reserve_fund.minimumAllocation: 10% of the balance remaining after provisions for items (i), (ii) and (iii)

coverage: Improvement of institution and connected buildings
clause_vi_construction_repairs_renovatio.threshold: Annual income is not less than ₹1,00,000
clause_vi_construction_repairs_renovatio.minimumAllocation: At least 30% of the balance remaining after provisions for items (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)

clause_b_common_good_fund.threshold: Annual income calculated under Section 65 exceeds ₹50,000
clause_b_common_good_fund.provision: Prescribed amount paid to the Common Good Fund (governed by Section 70)

part5_section_57_3_alteration_by_authori.power: Competent authority may alter, omit or add budget provisions.
mandatoryProcess: 1. Notice must be given to the trustee in the prescribed manner.
2. The trustee must have an opportunity to make a representation.
3. The authority must consider that representation.
4. The authority may then make the appropriate alterations, omissions or additions.

part6_section_57_4_revised_budget.purpose: Submitted during the financial year if modification is necessary for receipts or distribution.

actionRequired: 3. Report to the competent authority for possible ratification.

part8_high_yield_summary.rule: Budget submitted 90 days before close of financial year showing probable receipts and disbursements
Maintenance, services, remuneration & Dittam (Salaries <= 30% of Sec 65 income)
Pilgrim health, safety & convenience (Income > ₹20,000 -> >= 40% of balance after i-iii)
Reserve fund = 10% of balance after i-iii
Construction/repairs (Income >= ₹1 lakh -> >= 30% of balance after i-iv)
Income > ₹50,000 -> provision for prescribed Common Good Fund payment
Notice and representation required before budget alteration
Revised budget cannot affect allocations for liabilities and working balance
Excess expenditure reported forthwith with reasons; may be ratified

part9_key_numbers.90_days: Budget submission deadline before financial year end
part9_key_numbers.30_percent_salaries: Maximum establishment salary allocation against Sec 65 income
part9_key_numbers.20000_rupees: Income threshold for pilgrim health/safety 40% provision
part9_key_numbers.40_percent: Minimum provision for pilgrim health/safety against specified balance
part9_key_numbers.10_percent: Reserve fund contribution against specified balance
part9_key_numbers.30_percent_repairs: Minimum construction/repairs provision against specified balance
part9_key_numbers.50000_rupees: Income threshold for Common Good Fund budget provision

part10_common_mcq_traps.q: What period does the budget cover?

part10_common_mcq_traps.a: 90 days before close of financial year.
Balance remaining after items (i), (ii) and (iii), NOT gross income.

finalMemoryLine: 90 days -> 30% salaries -> 40% pilgrim provision -> 10% reserve -> 30% repairs -> ₹50,000 Common Good Fund threshold -> notice before alteration -> liabilities and working balance protected -> excess reported forthwith.
